faqs.question: What is Jewellery Designing?
faqs.answer: Jewelry design is art or profession of designing and creating jewelry . This is one of civilization's earliest forms of decoration, dating back at least 7000 years to oldest known human societies in Mesopotamia and Egypt. faqs.question: What is gemology?
faqs.answer: Gemology is a scientific study that is concerned with gemstones. These gemstones could be natural or artificial. Gemology is a significant part of Jewellery Design as the Designer has to recognise and analyse gemstones before using them in jewellery. On becoming a licensed and certified gemologist one can evaluate and certify gemstones. Richard T. Liddicoat is regarded as the father of modern gemology. Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald are considered to be the big three gemstones. The blue diamond is the most precious gemstone. Hope this helps!!!

faqs.question: Is Jewellery Design subject a part of Fashion Design?
faqs.answer: Yes, Jewellery Design is a sub-field in the Fashion Design stream. Fashion Design is a broad field covering Jewellery Design, Apparel Design, Footwear Design, Knitwear Design, Textile Design, and so on. Hope this helps!!!

Upcoming Trends in Jewellery Design

Irregular Hoops - Hoops that are not perfect, but exude personality and character can be a great addition to one's jewellery collection. Make sure that the hoops look youthful, and modern, and have an element of playfulness (in the way it hangs, sways and moves).
Mismatched diamonds - Diamonds with a mixed, quirky cut is also a current trend. These mismatched pieces will allow the wearer to add personality and make a unique, but subtle style statement.
Include a statement piece - After being under the shadow and gloom created by the COVID pandemic, people are again ready to make a big style statement, even if it is flashy.
So, barely there jewellery is giving way to more on-your-face statement jewellery. If you still haven’t jumped on the bandwagon, you ought to!

Sustainable jewellery - According to the State of Fashion report, up to 30% of jewellery purchases by 2025 will be done considering the sustainability of the piece. So, any budding designer must also incorporate the sustainability element in their future designs.
Scope of Jewellery Design in India

The gems and jewellery industry is one of the fastest growing sectors in India, with current merchandise export standing at around 10-12%, while the sector contributed around 7% to the GDP, as per data published by the India Brand Equity Foundation (IBEF).
In 2021-22, export of Indian gems and jewelley reached US $39.14 billion, up more than 54.13% from the previous year.
India also has the distinction of being the top exporter of cut and polished diamonds, and second in gold jewellery, silver jewellery, and lab-grown diamonds.
So, it can be safely said that Jewelley design is one of the hottest career choices for students out there!

questions.question_text: Is TDV good for Interior Design? Looking for honest feedback on faculty, studio culture, projects and overall learning experience.

answers.answer_text: I'm studying Interior Design here, and what stands out is that you're in the studio almost all the time. You don't just submit work and forget it — you keep reworking the same design after feedback, which really improves your thinking. Faculty push you a lot, sometimes it feels annoying, but later you realise why. The studio culture is intense near submissions, but very chill otherwise. You learn less from lectures and more from mistakes, discussions, and long studio hours. It's not fancy or easy, but if you stay involved, you genuinely improve.
